title: Clarification about first condition in replay protection implementation

nodes.body:
Yes, this looks weird. I'll take a closer look. It may be historical...

I remember at some point my replay protection code had the high bit set for specific packet types that had sequence numbers, but shouldn't have replay protection applied to them. I'm not sure if this still applies to netcode.io protocol though.

If you disable this check, do the netcode.io tests still pass?

cheers

- Glenn

Hi Glenn, 

Thanks for taking a look. I can't test it atm since I'm in the middle of implementing it from scratch (getting a real thorough understanding of the problem/solution) but I'll appreciate it if you can confirm its usefulness or lack there of. I'll leave it out for now.

Thanks
- Stef
Awesome. What language are you in? Also, feel free to continue asking me any questions you have as you implement.

OK. I removed the weird check, fixed a failing test (looking to verify this high bit behavior was there), and then every other test passed.

I think it is historical, and I've checked in a fix to remove it.

cheers

- Glenn

Right on, thanks for looking into it. 

To answer your question I'm in C# for Unity, but in a much more "data oriented" (if you wanna call it that) way with intent to move it to jai when Thekla gets around to releasing that. 

- Stef

Great stuff. Are you planning on sharing your implementation open source? I'd be happy to link to it and publicize it, even if it's a work in progress.

cheers

- Glenn

I can certainly share it when its done, but I am taking some liberties with the assumption that it's for personal use so it may not be exactly to spec. For example I'm disregarding the seperation of "netcode.io" and reliability. 

I dont think I'm exactly qualified to be releasing libraries but I'll share as an example regardless.
Ahhhhh this is like what SuperNetcode.io is doing as well in C#...
